title: Agent37 (YC F26)
summary: Low-cost agent sandboxes for running agents

extra.author: vishnukool
extra.original_title: Launch HN: Agent37 (YC F26) – Low-cost agent sandboxes for running agents

story_text.value:
Hey HN, I’m Vishnu from Agent37 (https://agent37.com). We build sandboxes for running AI agents at under 10% of the cost of most sandbox providers. Our customers spend an average of $0.37/month per sandbox.

You can view a video walkthrough of the product here: https://youtu.be/DK5ISR2tbNo

We started as one of those OpenClaw wrapper companies back in February (yup.. judge me). In time we added more and more harnesses.

One of the goals I had at the time was to offer a free plan to users, so as to gain more market share. But it was too cost prohibitive to do it right away. Especially since we were bootstrapped and servers were running on my savings.

Today we’re actually able to offer the free plan thanks to the optimizations we’ve made since. Over 90% of the new signups we have are just free plan users and they host their personal Hermes/Openclaw/Claude Code etc on our cloud. Our infrastructure cost for the free sandboxes averages around $0.05 to $0.10 per user per month.

Here are some techniques that have worked for lowering cost:

* When you look at agent harnesses, they have certain patterns in the way they consume CPU and RAM. They need CPU in bursts when they’re initializing or performing certain tasks, but beyond that, they’re often not peaking. They need more RAM for things like browser and computer-use tasks. Once the task is done, usage often comes back down. This is a key insight in lowering cost, so by efficiently managing the CPU/RAM utilization we could lower the cost.

* Secondly, you have to skip the hyperscalers when renting the Hosts. I worked at Amazon before and they have 80-90% margins on VMs. So it was an obvious choice once I looked at the prices to go one layer down to vendors like Hetzner and OVH. This alone was probably one of the biggest cost levers in reducing the cost.

* Thirdly, you also want to pick a technology stack that lets you efficiently cache and share resources across the host. We use gVisor for better utilization and fast boot times. It lets us use available host memory across sandboxes without reserving a full VM’s memory for each one. There are tradeoffs: our gVisor sandboxes don’t support workloads like Docker-in-Docker or Android emulators.

* And finally the size and shape of the hosts you buy also makes a big difference. RAM is typically the bottleneck when it comes to cost and not the CPU. This is specifically true for agent harness workloads, so when buying servers, we optimize for packing more RAM into a given host.

We also host full VM sandboxes for workloads that need them, including running Docker at a slightly higher price, but they are still pretty low cost given the rest of the techniques.

Overall, my learning has been that just by focusing on a niche of sandbox usecases, and optimizing for it you can give a much better cost/performance tradeoff.

I was previously a Senior Software Engineer at Amazon and an Engineering Manager at Quantcast. I built Amazon's internal AI chatbot, Diya, and their internal coding harness, Ziya.

If you’re someone who’s looking to run agents on sandbox and are exploring a sandbox vendor, come check us out. We’re particularly looking for developers building messaging agents to try their workloads and challenge the limits and economics of our platform.

Thanks!

https://agent37.com

For example, premium datasets charge by the query, research APIs meter by the call, and paywalled publishers gate content behind payment. When an AI agent encounters one of these resources, the server returns HTTP 402 Payment Required. The agent has no built-in payment mechanism, no budget attached to the session, and no programmatic way to satisfy the request. The task stalls and requires manual intervention. Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments handles machine-to-machine payment workflows on behalf of the agent. Developed in collaboration with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center Partner Agent Factory , it’s now available on AWS Marketplace . This post covers how Anchor Browser integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments so that AI agents can pay for x402-protected pages and APIs autonomously. The x402 protocol is an open standard for HTTP-based machine-to-machine payments. A server responds with 402 Payment Required along with the amount, accepted payment methods, and payment address that the agent uses to complete the transaction. Querying that data required precise model names, nested relationship navigation, and selection from 18 operators (comparison functions like equals or contains used to filter results). To reclaim it, the ShipStation Global Engineering team built Deckhand , an AI-powered IT help desk agent for Slack, on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore . ShipStation Global is the leading intelligent shipping and logistics platform for small and mid-sized shippers, and it operates on a simple belief: the more efficient its teams are, the better it delivers for customers. title: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
summary: SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, which offers a choice of foundation models (FMs) from multiple providers. According to SpaceXAI, Grok 4.7 is trained to work longer on more difficult tasks and knows when to check its own work. That matters most for agents, which carry a task through many steps and must verify what they find along the way. An agent that works this way has to do more than look things up. It has to form a candidate answer, check it against what it has learned, and refine it until it fits. Grok 4.7 exposes a reasoning effort setting that controls how much deliberation happens before each response, and for agent workloads a practical question is which level to run. In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three tasks that require search rather than lookup. The tasks are diagnosing a two-service outage from its alerts, scheduling maintenance under interacting constraints, and choosing an optimal set of migrations under a budget. Each task has exactly one correct answer, verified by brute force. We ran all three at every reasoning effort level, six times each, for 72 agent runs.

title: Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a sparsely-activated architecture that scales large language model (LLM) capacity while keeping per-token compute low. Because its operations account for a large share of total compute time, inefficiencies there directly raise request latency and cost. Therefore, optimizing MoE operations through kernel engineering offers the largest opportunity for performance gains. Fused MoE is a key optimization technique for the MoE architecture. A fused MoE system merges token routing, data shuffling, and specialized network calculations into a single batched operation on the GPU. This replaces executing those routing and expert computations as separate, sequential loop operations. While this provides latency advantages, it also brings complexity in kernel implementations and debugging capability. High GPU utilization for this architecture requires hardware-specific optimizations. In this post, we describe the different kernel optimizations we implemented for fused MoE models and show you how you can benefit from this work. We used a representative MoE model as our primary example. This post shows you how to configure the call, set permissions, and monitor inference from your source Region. GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, and GPT-6 Astra are all available through global cross-Region inference from the preceding Regions, on the bedrock-runtime endpoint. See Cross-Region inference in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide. For the full list of source and destination Regions in each profile, see Supported Regions and models for inference profiles . In this post, we introduce the global cross-Region inference profiles and invoke them from Asia Pacific (Singapore) using the Converse API, the OpenAI-compatible APIs, and coding clients. We then cover the AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) and service control policy (SCP) configuration, quota management, and monitoring. title: Deploy decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI
summary: Applications that route requests, select agent actions, or assign policy outcomes often need scores over a fixed set of choices instead of free-form text. Deploying these decision models with llama.cpp on Amazon SageMaker AI gives you a managed path for serving quantized models on CPU or GPU infrastructure. This post continues a series on specialized AWS Deep Learning Containers (DLCs) for generative AI inference. Previous posts cover WhisperX , vLLM-Omni – Part 1 , and vLLM-Omni – Part 2 . In this post, you first use the AWS DLC for llama.cpp to serve OpenAI-compatible chat completions through SageMaker AI InvokeEndpoint . You then extend the same runtime with SemIf , formerly OpenJev, which returns probabilities over declared options without decoding an answer token. The accompanying code sample includes CPU and GPU deployment options. Solution overview Figure 1 shows two deployment paths from the same packaged model. The text-generation path uses the AWS DLC for llama.cpp and returns generated responses through the OpenAI-compatible API. The structured-decision path builds a child image that replaces the default server with a SemIf adapter and returns probabilities for declared options. title: Run multi-node inference workloads using Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers
summary: This post shows how to deploy one large language model (LLM) across two GPU nodes on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with the multi-node Ray LLM Deep Learning Containers . It uses separate prefill and decode nodes behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This kind of multi-node setup is common for tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism, as well as prefill/decode disaggregation inference workloads. In a previous post , we introduced the Ray Serve DLC and used it to stand up a small model behind an HTTP endpoint on a single GPU node. You had a working inference endpoint, and the container keeps the GPU stack compatible, including CUDA libraries, so you did not need to write boilerplate code. Ray is a distributed compute framework, so Ray Serve deployments can span multiple nodes. Customers use multi-node Ray Serve for several reasons. Some want to run foundation or open-weight models that are too large for a single GPU. Others need more throughput than one replica can deliver. Still others want to separate the two phases of inference to improve performance. summary: For most languages of the world, language model pre-training operates in a data-constrained regime where models must repeat their training data many times, degrading generalization. Two remedies exist: aggressive hyperparameter tuning such as high weight decay, and mixing in data from a high-resource auxiliary language to directly aid the low-resource target. With MT evaluation spanning a large number of language pairs, domains and levels of annotation granularity, LLMs must be thoroughly evaluated across these dimensions before being reliably used as alternatives to human evaluation. title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: How to teach Copilot about your codebase
summary: Context matters when you’re working with AI. Every codebase has its own house rules: how components are structured, which scripts to run, and which conventions apply to different frameworks and file types. Copilot can help you make changes across a project, but it works best when it knows those rules, too. Much of that knowledge can live inside the repository, so Copilot can pick it up automatically instead of requiring you to explain the same standards, scripts, and workflows every time you start a new task. In this installment of our GitHub Copilot app for Beginners series, we’ll look at four ways to tailor how Copilot works with your project: Custom instructions communicate the conventions Copilot should follow. Agent skills package repeatable procedures. Custom agents bring specialized guidance to larger tasks. Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers connect Copilot to external tools and data sources, expanding what it can do. Let’s look at how each one works and how they can work together. Start with custom instructions Suppose you ask Copilot to add a custom page size to an application. Making the change is only part of the job. The new code should also follow the patterns your team already uses.

Apple Watch 走近门时，门锁可以自动解锁。 摄像头可回看 10 天事件录像，但需要符合条件的 iCloud+ 订阅。配件从 12 月起陆续上市，部分要等到 2027 年初；美国市场室内摄像头 199.95 美元起，门锁 349.95 美元起。首发市场为美国、加拿大，摄像头还包括英国，尚未公布中国大陆销售安排。 从这套配件能看出，苹果希望一起简化的，还有用户把家里的设备接进系统、日后再统一管理的过程。 门锁、摄像头与温控器一起加入｜图片来源：Apple 这块共享屏幕也能认出正在使用它的用户是谁：它最多能通过面部识别 6 位家庭成员，每个人都可以拥有自己的主屏幕、App 和小组件。 苹果产品页写明了个人内容的显示条件：HomeView 认出这个人的脸，同时他配对的 iPhone 或 iPad 连在同一个 Wi-Fi 下并且最近解锁过，信息、日历这类内容才会出现。Siri AI 要调用某个人的日程、信息等个人上下文，也需要这个人有一台支持 Apple Intelligence 的 iPhone 或 iPad 与 HomeView 配对。 同一块屏幕切换不同人的主屏｜图片来源：Apple 这些条件管的只是个人内容，并不限制谁能用这块屏幕。苹果在说明中表示，家人即使没有支持 Apple Intelligence 的设备，也能用到 Siri AI 的广泛世界知识、自然对话和音乐推荐。访客和未被识别的人可以控制家居配件、查天气、设定计时器、放音乐，只是看不到任何人的个人信息。对成员多、手机新旧不一的家庭来说，这样的分法比较贴近实际。 一块装着摄像头和麦克风、摆在客厅里的屏幕，隐私是绕不开的问题 。苹果给出的方案是 A18 芯片里的 Secure Exclaves：摄像头和麦克风数据在一个隔离的运行环境里处理，苹果称 HomeView 的软件、App、用户和苹果自己都无法访问这部分数据。需要上云的 Siri 请求走私有云计算，苹果承诺这些数据既不会被存储，也不会被包括苹果在内的任何人访问。 娱乐方面，HomeView 能播放 Apple Music、播客以及兼容的第三方音视频 App。这些功能集中在家庭使用场景，不能把它当成一台可任意安装 iPad 应用的平板。 第四代 Apple TV 4K 的美国售价为 299 美元，同样 11 月 13 日上市 。它换上了 A19 芯片，机身里加了 3 个远场麦克风，看剧时不用摸遥控器，就能直接叫 Siri。 苹果为 Apple TV

title: 说个事：极客公园创新大会 2027！
summary: 一年一度：极客公园创新大会 2027，已经启动了。 你大概已经注意到一些不太寻常的事——科技行业真正关心的东西，一直在变。 大模型公司的关注点，过去几年，几个月就一波变化：从追求用户规模，到追求技术的 SOTA 程度；应用公司的产品热点从 Chatbot，到 Agent，再到 Personal Agent；生产力工具也从 Copilot，一路到了 workspace。甚至连工程领域的概念也在快速更迭，从 Prompt Engineering，已经到了到 Environment Engineering。 流行概念的交替，实质是科技领域里，创新问题的权重和价值，正在被快速重估。什么值得投入、什么人更重要、什么样的能力还能构成壁垒——答案已经不是过去的答案。 经过这几年 AI 带来的冲击和对世界的影响，我们已经可以清晰地看到：一次根本性的价值重估已经开始。 有的公司在长出惊天市值，有的公司在被彻底遗忘；有人好像在丢掉岗位，但有人正在变成「超人」；技术、产品、组织和人，都在重新给出关于「价值」的新答案。 时代从不预告它的转向，只是沉默地重新衡量一切。 今年，极客公园创新大会 2027（IF 2027）想讨论的，就是这件事。陪你一起，在这个重新估值的时代里，找到属于自己的坐标与上升通道。 极客公园创新大会每一年的主题，都是那个时代脉搏的共振。我们习惯在热点还没形成的时候，把那个时代最迫切真实的问题，提前摆上台面，变成一场大会的主题。 这么多年，一直如此。 2017 年，AlphaGo 点燃了全球对 AI 的想象，以技术变化的加速时代开始到来。那一年，我们的主题是「科技主义」——就算那时候大家还在谈移动互联网，我们依旧把那些相信技术、尊重技术、用技术改变世界的人请上台。 2019 年，移动互联网退潮让整个行业集体收缩、观望，很多人都在问「还能怎么办」。那一年，我们的主题是「WHY NOT」——有一些人看到世界可能的样子，会思考「为什么不能更好一些？」今天的智能电动车、自动驾驶和大模型、机器人恰恰来自于那些当时喊出「why not」的团队。 2023 年，ChatGPT 们第一次让 AI 成为普通人手里的工具。AI 开始涌现出技术革命的浪潮。那一年，我们的主题是「增强人生」——我们看到的是科技开始增强每一个个体，不仅仅是更省心，更好用，而是可以让我们突破原来的能力和资源桎梏去撒欢儿。 2025 年，AI 已经开始体现出解决问题的更大能力，真正的稀缺变成了人如何设定目标、判断和行动。那一年，我们的主题是「进程由我 On The Loop！」——技术是阶梯，但主动权，必须拿在自己的手中。 今年也一样。 你可以看到，商业世界，甚至整个社会的价值结构，正在发生确定性的变化—— 创新和价值的权重在快速转移，不是所有东西都变贵了，也不是所有努力都还值钱。答案正在被重写。 因此，这也成为了我们今年大会的主题： Revaluation 价值，另有答案 所以今年，我们决定站在这个视角：既看懂 2026 年正在发生的事，也看清未来 18 个月里，哪些是值得你投身的方向？究竟什么正在变得更加贵重？哪些事情更值得你去改变？ 这场跨越全球的价值重估，无人能够置身事外。它已经开始， 这就是为何你一定要来 IF 2027 的原因。 找到那些跑赢时代的人，极客公园已经干了十几年。 2010 年，北京朝阳公园，索尼探梦科技馆的地下室。两把大红沙发椅，周围四五十个人席地而坐，大多是一脸理工气息的工程师和产品经理。王兴、雷军、张一鸣、周源——这些后来改变中国互联网格局的名字，当时就坐在那里。 那一年，我们办了第一届中国互联网创新产品评选——也就是后来 InnoAwards 和 IF 大会的前身。小米、美团、微信、字节跳动、大疆，这些如今如雷贯耳的公司，在极早期都曾率先出现在极客公园的舞台上。 IF，是一群 Doer（行动者）的聚会。 每年都有无数人克服遥远与疲惫，肉身来到 IF 的现场。 我们深知，愿意在这个快节奏的时代里，挤出时间、亲临现场的人，内心深处一定有着更高的山峰想要去攀登，有着不愿向庸常妥协的野心。 在现场，你会被那群人感染。听最硬核的思想碰撞，摸最前沿的产品。看清世界，照见自己。你身边左右的人，也可能成为你未来的朋友、合伙人，甚至对手。 然后带着一份安定感与清醒，重新踏上征程。 今年的大会，既是对 2026 年的观察总结，也是面向未来 18 个月的下注和断言。为了这场真诚的碰撞，IF 2027 将用四个半天，为你梳理出接下来的航向： Day1 上午「非共识」追问 Keep Asking 那些当年顶着嘲讽与质疑下注、如今带着成绩归来的「非共识者」，听他们讲讲当年的抉择，以及最新的重注。 Day1 下午 跑赢时代 Level Up with AI 当个体开始跑赢老板，小团队开始跑赢大公司，那些真正跑出结果的人、提供底层「军火」的人，如何重新定义今天的人力与组织。 Day2 上午 未来 500 天 Frontier Bets 具身智能、RSI、自动驾驶……告别宏大的 PPT，只讲未来 500 天内兑现的断言，现场连线硅谷与最敏锐的投资人。 Day2 下午 新产品，超体验 New Things，New Senses 能用双手亲手触摸到的 AI 硬件、具身机器人，以及那些天马行空的 Maker 与新匠人现场局。 同样，我们今年也在主舞台的外面，搭起了更多 「小场深谈」 ： 这是一个个思考据点，嘉宾、观众面对面，一个主题，3 个小时的深入探讨。你可以提出自己的问题，成为一场讨论的共同创作者。 展区也会更侧重趋势：AI 硬件、具身智能、Maker 与新匠人，看得见，上得了手。将技术、产品和商业放在一起，或许能让我们更接近答案。 时代的重估浪潮里，英雄不问出处。 极客公园正在寻找那些在这场风暴中，提前跑出结果、找到向上阶梯的 Outlier，集结新面孔和年轻力量。 如果你正带领团队用全新的 AI 工作流，撬动着成倍的生产力； 如果你的产品正打破旧逻辑，创造出全新的价值； 如果你对接下来 500 天的商业与技术演进，有着坚决且被验证过的断言…… 请告诉我们，IF 2027 的舞台为你而留。我们诚挚地邀请你加入这场集结，与我们一起在这个岁末，为所有在路上的 Doer 输出方向。 可以联系你身边的极客公园的同事，或者发送你的介绍到邮箱 bd@geekpark.net。 特别预告 老朋友们都知道，极客公园创新大会的门票，几乎每年都会在会前提前售罄。去年即便临时加票，依然让不少关注 IF 的朋友抱憾未能来到现场。 如果你依然相信极客公园对科技脉搏的敏锐觉察，如果你也想在岁末年终，为自己寻找一份面向未来的确定性与安定感： IF 2027 官方门票将于 11 月初开售，请及时留意「极客公园」公众号，或有限量早鸟优惠票掉落哦～提早锁定，真正踏实。 价值重估已经开始！ 12 月 5 日 - 6 日 ，来 IF 2027，寻找接下来 500 天值得相信的事。

title: 上线九个月下载破亿，字节在海外再造「红果」
summary: 头图来源：视觉中国 上线不到一年，字节跳动旗下的短剧 App PineDrama，累计下载量已经突破 1 亿次。 10 月 12 日，Sensor Tower 的一组数据让短剧赛道再添热度：字节跳动旗下海外短剧应用 PineDrama 累计下载量已突破 1 亿次，日活跃用户约 700 万，仅 2026 年 9 月单月下载量就超过 1200 万次。 距离这款产品正式上线，才刚过去 9 个月。在全球累计下载破亿的 7 款独立短剧 App 里，PineDrama 是唯一一款上线不足一年的新品。这让人很自然地联想到它的国内「前辈」——红果短剧，那个用三年时间做到日活 1.68 亿、超过四家长视频平台总和的现象级产品。 字节已经用红果在国内把免费短剧做成了大众娱乐产品，如今，它能否在海外再做一遍？ 从红果到 PineDrama：一套验证过的模式出海 PineDrama 的诞生，本身就是字节短剧战略的自然延伸。 2025 年 12 月，当国内的红果短剧已经跑出月活超 2 亿、单月播放量逼近百亿的成绩时，字节在海外悄然上线了这款独立短剧应用，首批落地巴西、美国、印尼等市场，支持 TikTok 账号一键登录。 从产品形态到商业模式，PineDrama 几乎是把红果的成功路径完整复刻了过去：全剧集免费观看、靠广告变现，搭配看剧领金币的轻激励机制，彻底拿掉了用户的付费门槛。 这和当时海外短剧市场的主流玩法完全不同。在 PineDrama 入场之前，ReelShort、DramaBox 等头部玩家普遍采用"前几集免费引流、后续单集付费解锁"的模式，靠用户充值打赏实现收入，本质上是把国内早期的付费短剧模式搬到了海外。 图片来源：TikTok PineDrama 选了一条更激进的路——用免费换规模。这背后是字节对自己流量体系的自信：用户在 TikTok 刷到几十秒的短剧高光片段，被强冲突的剧情抓住情绪，点一下链接就能跳转到 PineDrama 看全集，从种草到留存的整个获客闭环，几乎都在字节生态内部完成。 这套打法在国内已经被红果验证过。2023 年 8 月红果上线时，行业主流还是付费解锁，红果靠免费+广告的模式迅速起量，上线不到一年日活就突破 3000 万，2025 年春节期间累计观看人次达到 6 亿，甚至超过了同期全国电影春节档的观影人次。如今 PineDrama 在海外走的，几乎是一模一样的增长曲线。 9 个月破亿：新兴市场的爆发与本土化的支撑 数据层面，PineDrama 的增长速度确实足够亮眼。2026 年一季度它的下载量还只有 684 万次，二季度环比大增 460%，直接冲进 Sensor Tower 中国非游戏应用出海下载榜第七位，是榜单里上线时间最短的产品。到 8 月单月下载已经超过 1700 万次，9 月累计下载量正式突破 1 亿大关。 如果拆开市场结构看，这波增长的核心驱动力其实来自新兴市场。Sensor Tower 的数据显示，印尼和巴西两国合计贡献了 PineDrama 82%的累计下载量。在巴西，PineDrama 曾连续两个月压过 TikTok、WhatsApp 登顶当地应用商店总榜，印尼市场的表现也紧随其后。 图片来源：Sensor Tower 免费模式在这些市场杀伤力极强。对于付费意愿较低、对价格敏感的新兴市场用户来说，"不用花钱就能看完全集"的吸引力远大于"看几集就要付费解锁"的传统模式。 再加上 TikTok 在这些地区极高的渗透率，源源不断的流量灌入让 PineDrama 的用户规模像滚雪球一样越滚越大。AdMapix 的数据显示，PineDrama 在美国曝光量最高的创意素材仅拿到 71.9 万次曝光，却支撑起单日 172 万次下载—— 这种获客效率，是传统买量模型根本做不到的。 另一个容易被忽略的点是内容本土化。和很多出海短剧只是把国内剧本翻译一下就上线的做法不同，PineDrama 的内容以海外本土原创为主。比如尼日利亚本土故事《10 亿奈拉新娘》就成为了平台爆款，单部播放量破亿。用免费模式和 TikTok 流量扩大用户基本盘，再用本土内容承接用户的观看需求，构成了 PineDrama 目前清晰的增长路径。 复刻红果之后，变现能跟上吗？ 从上线时间维度来看，PineDrama 的增长效率很高，只用 9 个月就做到了 700 万日活，跑出了比国内不少「前辈」更快的起量速度。这也意味着，至少在用户增长层面，红果的免费流量打法在海外市场完全跑通了，规模扩张只是时间问题。 接下来的核心命题，其实是规模之后的商业化能不能达到红果的量级。 红果在国内能跑通免费模式，很大程度上依赖中国庞大且成熟的广告市场—— 行业估算红果 2025 年全年收入超过 150 亿元，2026 年单月广告收入就能达到 42 亿元。高企的广告 eCPM 和充足的广告主预算，撑起了「免费看剧 + 广告变现」的商业闭环。 而 PineDrama 当前的核心增长市场集中在印尼、巴西等新兴地区，这些市场的广告单价远低于国内，也远低于欧美成熟市场。用户规模扩张很快，但单用户广告价值的天花板要低得多。 这也是这套出海模式最受行业关注的地方：靠免费策略快速抢占用户盘子很容易，但在低广告价值市场，仅靠广告收入能否覆盖内容采购、流量投放和本土化运营的成本？毕竟即便是在国内市场，红果也依然处在「规模优先」的扩张阶段，而海外市场的媒体环境、广告生态更加分散复杂。 不过字节的打法向来如此—— 先用最高效的方式拿下市场份额，再逐步打磨商业化效率。从 TikTok 到抖音电商，这条路径已经被验证过多次。PineDrama 现在已经拿到了海外短剧市场的核心入场券，接下来要走的，正是红果在国内走过的路：从用户增长到内容生态，再到广告体系的逐步成熟。 至少从目前的增长势头来看，中国短剧的免费模式出海，第一步已经跑通了。至于能不能最终长成下一个红果量级的产品，答案或许不用等太久。

title: 复旦邱锡鹏团队获超 10 亿融资，成立两年，让模型感知、理解、响应变化的世界
summary: 大模型融资还在继续，新的押注转向了能边听、边看、边说的 AI。 作者｜Li Yuan 编辑｜ 郑玄 想象这样一个家庭场景。 孩子正在玩玩具，突然，厨房里「哐」的一声，玻璃碎了，紧接着传来孩子的声音：「不是我。」语速很快，尾音压得很低，有点紧张。两秒后，一只猫从厨房门口窜出来，钻进了沙发底下。 今天的模型，能分别识别这些信息。转写模型能记下孩子的话，音频模型能听出是玻璃碎裂，视觉模型能认出那只猫。但把这些能力叠在一起，模型仍然不知道刚才发生了什么。 那声脆响是从哪个方向来的？碎玻璃、那句急着撇清的「不是我」、逃窜的猫，是不是同一件事？厨房地上有没有碎片，孩子是不是正光着脚站在旁边？AI 需要把声音、画面、人物和前后发生的事情联系起来，在信息还不完整时作出判断，必要时继续观察或向人确认。 但这比识别一行命令、一段语音、一帧画面复杂得多。 过去几年，大模型越来越擅长处理被写进文档、代码和 Prompt 的世界。但这份能力有一个前提：有人先理解现实，再把它整理成模型读得懂的输入，模型随后完成推理和回答。进入真实世界以后，这两件事需要同时发生—— 模型既要持续理解一个仍在变化的现场，也要在现场继续发生时迅速回应，并根据新情况随时调整。 10 月 12 日，模思智能宣布完成超 10 亿元 Pre-A 轮融资，由华控基金领投，主要投资方包括国开科创、上海科创基金、新微资本、徐汇资本、追光硬科技创投、临港策源基金等，元禾控股、上海国投旗下上海科创集团、星连资本等老股东持续投资。这轮融资距离天使轮官宣只隔了半年左右。 这家由复旦大学 特聘教授、上海创智学院副院长 邱锡鹏 教授创立 、成立不到两年的公司，瞄准 的正是 这里，公司 将其定义为 构建情境智能。 「我对下一代 AI 的一个判断是，它会从回答问题走向持续在场。模型不只是等人输入，而是要持续理解人和环境，在合适的时候回应、行动。我们现在做全模态实时交互，就是在解决这件事。」邱锡鹏表示。 模思从声音开始，逐步拓展至视觉理解、音视频生成和实时交互。据公司披露，2026 年以来，它围绕语音、视觉和实时多模态连续发布了 20 多个模型，其中包括多个开源模型。其中 7 月开源的 MOSS-VL-Realtime 已经能持续接收视频流，画面一变，判断就跟着更新。 过去几年，大模型越来越擅长回答一个已经提出的问题；接下来，或许更它还要学会理解一个仍在变化的现场。 01 一个为自己造的模型，意外走到了前排 模思智能孵化自复旦大学邱锡鹏带领的 OpenMOSS 团队。这是国内最早的大模型团队之一。2023 年 2 月，ChatGPT 刚刚把大模型推到聚光灯下，邱锡鹏团队便发布了 MOSS，这是国内最早开源的类 ChatGPT 对话模型之一。 同年，团队开始探索多模态领域，2023 年，团队推出 SpeechGPT，尝试让模型直接理解和生成语音。2024 年，AnyGPT 又在探索如何完成统一的多模态大模型；2024 年 11 月，模思智能从 OpenMOSS 团队中孵化成立，开始用商业化的方式继续这场模型探索。 模思智能 CEO 李世民最初以学生身份加入邱锡鹏实验室，也是 SpeechGPT 的早期作者之一。极客公园造访模思位于上海的办公室时，这家公司仍保留着浓厚的 frontier lab 气质：全职员工一百多人，算法和研发人员占七到八成，00 后是团队的重要组成部分。 模思智能 CEO 李世民 ｜ 图片来源：模思 模思智能从成立之初想做的，就是下一代 AI：当模型进入汽车、智能硬件和机器人等真实终端，AI 要如何理解不断变化的现场，又该如何与物理世界实时交互。 当时，团队选择的第一个切口，是多人对话语音生成。 他们想做的 MOSS-TTSD，不是逐句合成声音，而是一次生成一段由两三个人参与、你来我往的完整播客。如果用普通 TTS 一句一句生成再拼接，对话里的气口、停顿、接话乃至抢话的节奏都会丢失。模思选择端到端生成，希望把一段对话完整的上下文和交叠节奏保留下来。 但要训练这样的模型，团队首先需要把大量真实对话拆解清楚：谁在什么时候说了什么，两个人何时接话，哪些声音发生了重叠。 这件事交给人并不难，模思却想尝试让模型来进行标注。结果却并不如意。 当时的常见方案是把语音识别和说话人分割交给不同模型，再沿着时间轴把结果拼回去。一旦录音变长，或者遇到多人插话、声音重叠，系统就容易把一句话安到错误的人头上。 「因为市面上没有满足要求的模型，我们就立项自研了。」李世民说。 2026 年 1 月，MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 第一版正式发布。 在他看来，模型之所以能够较早做到这一点，首先来自对问题的重新定义，MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 没有采取时间轴拼贴的方式，是当时首个能够在一次调用中，同时完成语音转写、说话人归属和时间戳预测的模型。 另一个原因是数据。团队使用了大量来自复杂场景的对话音频，再通过数据工程完成清洗、标注和训练。这让模型面对长录音、多人插话和声音重叠时，不只是在干净音频上识别文字，而是直接学习「谁在什么时候说了什么」。 这个为了训练另一个模型而造出的工具，效果超出了团队最初的预期。李世民 说 ，它很快达到了行业头部水平。 2026 年 1 月，团队公开了 MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 的技术报告。7 月 9 日，0.9B 参数版本正式开源，支持超过 50 种语言。五天后，它在 INTERSPEECH 2026 第二届 MLC-SLM Challenge 中获得第一名，比赛覆盖 14 种语言，共吸引 110 支队伍报名。 更让团队意外的是，需求也跟着找上门来。 有模型团队用它为训练数据做标注，也有企业把它用在客服、会议记录等对话场景里，其中不乏头部互联网公司的团队。 「这让我们意识到，模型能力的突破会自发激发出新的业务场景。」李世民说。 02 模型开始替模型工作 MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 并不是一个孤例。 模型不只是交付给用户的产品，也可以成为生产下一个模型的工具。 这逐渐变成模思反复使用的一种研发方式：遇到现有模型解决不了的问题，就自己造一个，并把这个单点问题做深。模型做出来后，一边进入外部场景，接住真实需求；一边回到内部，成为其他模型的数据来源、标注工具或评测手段。 沿着同样的方式，模思陆续做出了更多模型。转写解决的是「谁在什么时候说了什么」；MOSS-Audio 继续追问「这句话是怎么说的」，让模型识别语速、情绪、性别、言语卡顿和环境声音；MOSS-TTS 负责把文字重新变成可控的声音；到了视觉一侧，MOSS-VL 和 MOSS-VL-Realtime 又开始处理图像和持续进入的视频流。 MOSS 多模态模型矩阵 ｜ 图片来源：模思 在模思的办公室里，这些分工并不抽象。 产品负责人输入一段高铁广播词，回车刚刚敲下去，MOSS-TTS 生成的声音便开始播放。它不需要用户先上传一段参考录音，只要输入「一个年纪稍大的中年男性声音」，就能从文字描述中生成对应音色。 另一边，当接受这些录音的时候，用户可以直接问 MOSS-Audio：这个人说得快不快，带着什么情绪，是否出现了言语卡顿。传统转写会把这些信息丢掉，它试图把声音中没有被写成文字的部分重新捞回来。 而除此之外，模思表示，这些模型之间，正在彼此喂养。 一个理解模型可以为生成模型清洗和标注数据；生成模型造出新的语音、图像和视频，又可以交给理解模型筛选。标注过程中暴露出来的错误，会成为理解模型下一轮训练的材料；产品和客户返回的真实数据，则继续补上实验室数据没有覆盖的场景。 这里的标注不指给数据贴上几个简单标签。训练一个更可控的 TTS，模型需要知道一段声音里哪里在笑、哪里在哭，语气如何变化，韵律在哪里转折；训练视频生成模型，则需要把镜头运动、分镜、光影、人物动作和画面布局拆解出来。通用大模型可以给出大致描述，却未必能稳定产出这些细密、结构化，又能够直接用于训练的数据。 模思因此倾向于使用自己训练的理解模型，再把它们接入数据生产管线。 团队在采访中举了一个例子。 在音视频综合理解中，模型不仅要听懂说了什么，还要判断是谁在说话，以及声音与画面之间有怎样的联系。如果将音频和视觉信号分开处理，模型就可能在对应两者时出现偏差。 模思将自己训练的音视频理解模型接入这一环节，让同一个模型同时理解声音和画面，结合两种信号判断内容，减少信息割裂带来的误判和幻觉，为后续模型训练提供更可靠的数据。 一位模思的投资人表示，这正是他们选择投资模思的关键原因之一： 模思已经建立了一个模型帮助模型、模型校验模型的循环。模思把这套方式称为 AI for AI。 不同模型掌握着同一份数据的不同侧面，也可以拿各自的结果交叉印证。语音模型判断谁在说话，视觉模型判断画面里谁在动嘴，文本模型再检查内容和上下文是否一致。模型越多，未必意味着系统越散；如果它们能够彼此检查，反而可能更快暴露错误、筛掉低质量数据。 这套循环直接指向研发速度。 2026 年 4 月 7 日到 13 日的一周内，模思围绕 MOSS-VL 和 MOSS-Audio 连续迭代了 6 个版本。7 月初，团队又连续两天开源了 MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 0.9B 和实时视频理解模型 MOSS-VL-Realtime。 对一家初创公司来说，这套方式还有更现实的意义。复杂音视频如果依靠人工逐条描述，不仅很难扩展，速度也极其缓慢；如果全量调用商业闭源模型，成本又很快变得难以承受。模思因此用自研的轻量级理解模型承担大部分标注，再在关键节点加入人工精标和修正。 团队称，在一些具体任务上，这套管线不仅成本更低，结果也比直接调用通用模型更准确。原因是他们可以针对说话人对应、密集 OCR 等问题加入专门模型，再通过校验和过滤不断修正结果。 用更少的人、更低的成本生产更细的数据，再把这些数据更快送回训练，才是模思所谓 AI for AI 最直接的价值。 03 Omni model，还没有走到终点 到现在，模思手里已经有了一组分工明确的模型：MOSS-Transcribe-Diarize 负责判断谁在什么时候说了什么，MOSS-Audio 继续识别语速、情绪和环境声音，MOSS-VL-Realtime 持续接收正在变化的视频流，MOSS-TTS

title: 曝梁文锋密集见机器人创业者；影石出货量累计突破1000万台；Meta发布Muse Wonder模型｜极客早知道
summary: 曝梁文锋密集接触具身智能创业者，DeepSeek 拟入局具身智能 据报道，DeepSeek 创始人梁文锋近期密集关注具身智能领域，并与多位该领域创业者交流，探讨机器人、大模型与现实世界交互等方向。 据知情人士透露，梁文锋正在考虑 DeepSeek 进入具身智能领域的可能性，可能会亲自组建团队下场研发，也可能通过投资相关企业切入。 此前，梁文锋已投资宇树科技，另据彭博社报道，DeepSeek 计划领投腾讯前 AI 科学家胡瀚创立的机器人公司 Winverse AI。（来源：新浪科技） Meta 发布 Muse Wonder 模型，拥有主动记忆和主动专注功能，瞄准个人超级智能 Meta 今天推出 Muse Wonder 系列，包括 Muse Wonder 和 Muse Wonder Full 两款功能最强大的型号，它们在个人和专业智能任务中均能提供卓越的性能。它们的推出标志着我们产品线的又一次飞跃，也是迈向个人超智能的重大一步。Muse Wonder 融合了 主动记忆 和 主动专注功能 ，能够帮助您追踪重要事项，并高效地朝着目标努力。 Muse Wonder 现已可通过 Meta Model API 和 Muse Code 使用，Muse Wonder Full 现已面向 Muse Code 订阅用户推出。 Muse Wonder 即将为 Muse 中的各种体验提供支持，并将首先面向订阅用户推出。Muse Wonder 还将为需要更高智能的工件生成和流程提供支持。未来，Meta 将利用 Muse Wonder 开发专用模型，供所有 Muse 用户使用。（来源：Meta） 影石出货量累计突破 1000 万台 全景相机占比超 60% 10 月 13 日消息， 影石 Insta360 对外公布，旗下相机产品全球累计出货量已经突破 1000 万台，全景相机占整体出货超过 60% ，11 年时间做到这个规模，增长速度相当可观。 比较有意思的是， 1000 万台的总量里面，有 470 万台是过去 12 个月卖出去的，差不多接近一半。 也就是说影石最近一年的销量，几乎等于前面十年的总和，增长势头很猛。 相关庆祝活动之前已经在代工厂立讯精密的工厂完成，双方创始人以及工厂员工一起见证这个里程碑。 全景相机依旧是影石的基本盘。IDC 给出的数据显示，它在全球全景相机市场份额达到 72.5%，差不多每卖出去 10 台全景相机，就有 7 台来自影石。很多骑行、滑雪、旅行爱好者，都喜欢用全景相机，拍完之后再选画面，不用拍摄的时候纠结构图。（来源：快科技） 蚂蚁「灵光」开启小范围内测，新版对标「Meta Muse」 蚂蚁集团旗下 AI 产品「灵光」已于近日开启新版本的小范围内测，新版对标「Meta Muse」。 公开信息显示，今年 9 月，Meta 推出个人智能体 Muse。该智能体可介入用户日常生活，并持续跟进用户交待的事宜。 接近项目人士透露，灵光相关方向约半年前已开始筹备，期间迭代多个版本，计划本月全面开放。 该人士还透露，此次升级的核心，是灵光从能聊天、能生成应用的 AI 助手，转向拥有长期记忆、可主动推进任务的 AI 原生个人智能体。灵光新版本还能通过调用 Skill 和 MCP，实现钉钉发信息、调用智能家居设备等功能。 据悉，灵光 2.0 的内测用例集中在长程、变量多、普通人难盯住的场景，例如帮上班族跟踪市场异动、帮家长管理钉钉打卡、旅行中遇航班延误或景区限流重排路线等。（来源：新浪科技） 阶跃旗舰模型接入腾讯 WorkBuddy，限免 2 周 10 月 12 日下午消息，腾讯旗下全场景 AI 办公工作台 WorkBuddy 已接入阶跃最新旗舰模型 Step 5 Preview。即日起，该模型在 WorkBuddy 独家限时免费开放两周。凭借推理与 Agent 能力，Step 5 Preview 将帮 WorkBuddy 用户处理深度研究、信息检索、数据分析、文档与 PPT 生成等办公任务，并支持多步骤复杂任务的持续执行。 Step 5 Preview 是阶跃发布的新一代旗舰基座模型，面向 AI 编程、软件工程、专业知识工作及金融等场景进行了优化，并在旗舰级综合智能、效率与成本间实现了最佳平衡。模型采用稀疏 MoE 架构，总参数量达 6000 亿，每个 Token 激活约 270 亿参数。 据全球权威大模型评测榜单 Artificial Analysis 显示，其综合智能指数为 44 分，位居全球开源前三。此外，上周 Step 5 Preview 登顶 OpenRouter Trending 榜首，并在按 Token 使用量统计的日榜中排名全球第二，模型性能和开发者使用量不断提升。（来源：新浪科技） 存储短缺冲击，全球三季度手机出货量暴跌 20%：创 14 年来同期最低 市场调研机构 Counterpoint Research 表示，AI 基础设施建设持续挤占存储芯片供应，消费电子产业正面临成本与供应双重压力。初步数据显示，2026 年第三季度全球智能手机出货量同比下降 20%，降至 2012 年以来同期最低水平。 存储芯片危机已连续第二个季度对智能手机市场造成全面冲击，芯片成本上涨推高整机物料清单成本，加剧供应短缺，为转嫁成本压力厂商陆续上调终端售价，2026 年以来全球智能手机零售价格累计上涨约 20%。 三星继续稳居首位，第三季度市场份额升至 23%，出货量同比下降 3%，是主要厂商中份额增幅最大的企业。苹果市场份额升至 22%，第三季度首次突破 20%，iPhone 18 Pro 系列在中国和印度市场表现强于前代。小米第三季度出货量同比下降超过

title: 一周 10 万星，AI「逆向一切」，但大家不要过于兴奋
summary: 头图图片来源：REA 头图来源：CyberSecurityNews 「在应用里看到一个想加入自己产品的功能？让智能体去帮你调查它。」 这是 REA 项目主页第一屏的话。后半句更直接：即使没有源代码，智能体也可以检查应用、解释功能怎么工作、展示证据，「并为你的项目实现类似功能」。 REA 全名 Reverse Engineer Anything，即「逆向一切」。 上周它在 AI 开发者圈刷了屏：10 月 6 日还不到 1 万星，到 10 月 12 日已经超过 11 万 。 6 天涨了 10 万星，平均每天约 1.7 万｜图片来源：Star History 真正让普通人看到这件事的，是游戏。10 月初，一批老游戏突然能在浏览器里直接玩了：《光环：战斗进化》《半条命》《暗黑破坏神》，还有真正意义上的 3A 大作《GTA5》和《使命召唤：现代战争 2》。 其中最出圈的一份复盘，来自逆向开发者 Maurice Heumann：他让十几个 Claude Code 和 Codex 智能体并行干活，把一款射击游戏 99% 的函数还原成了 C++ 源码，其中 83% 编译出来和原程序逐字节一致。他用的是 Hex-Rays 的官方 MCP，不是 REA。 也就是说，REA 只是这波浪潮里名字最响的那一个。 同一个星期，整个 AI 逆向圈都在加速。 似乎，人人都有免费软件用、免费游戏玩的日子到来了。 旧工具，新用户 逆向工程，就是手里没有源代码，从编译好的程序往回推，搞清楚它是怎么写的。这原本是安全研究员和破解者的手艺：在反编译器、反汇编器、调试器之间来回切，一个功能拆上几天是常事。 REA 干的事，是把这套工具接到 AI 编程智能体上。接口用的是 MCP，一种让 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 这类智能体调用外部工具的通用协议。 装好之后，你对智能体说一句「弄清这个应用的搜索功能怎么工作」，它会自己去调 Ghidra、IDA 或 Hopper 等对应的工具，帮你翻二进制，调 JADX 拆安卓安装包，或者直接读 Electron 应用里打包的 JavaScript，最后把结论和证据一起交回来。 智能体负责提问，REA 负责取证｜图片来源：REA 听上去像个新物种。但放在专业圈里看，它其实更像一次重新包装：毕竟让 AI 接上逆向工具，GhidraMCP、IDA Pro MCP 这些开源项目去年就在做了。 REA 走红前不久，IDA Pro MCP 的作者、调试器 x64dbg 的开发者 Duncan Ogilvie 在 X 上说，他用 IDA 的 MCP 插件，大约一小时解完了今年 Flare-On 的全部题目。 Flare-On 是谷歌旗下 FLARE 团队每年办的逆向挑战赛，题目大多取材自真实的恶意软件分析。 这并非个例，逆向领域的专家们其实普遍对今天这波新兴起的浪潮不是很看得上眼：Elias Bachaalany 是逆向工程教材《Practical Reverse Engineering》的合著者，早年在 IDA 的开发商 Hex-Rays 工作过。 REA 被各路人马转发刷屏时，他也转了其中一条推介，开头就一个词：炒作。接着他列了几个早就存在的同类工具，意思是这些人只是没见过。 逆向教材合著者的评价，开头就一个词｜图片来源：X AI 能拆程序是真的，只是不从 REA 开始。能拆到什么程度，圈内说法也不一致。 安全领域博主轩辕之风认为，没加壳的程序 AI 轻松拿下，轻度加壳也行，VMP 这类高强度虚拟化保护目前还啃不动；他还批评 REA 连动态调试都没有。一家做逆向产品的公司也在 X 上说，碰到加壳样本，模型分析照样会卡住。反方的说法是：混淆能拖慢 AI，挡不住它。 公开的案例，多数落在容易的那一头。宝玉用 Codex 加 REA 逆向了一个混淆过的网页前端，说几乎完整还原了里面的编辑器。也有博主拿它拆剪映，发现 Claude 拆到一半会卡住，也会被限制。 还有一类东西，它怎么都拿不到：放在服务器上的逻辑。你能拆开装在自己电脑上的客户端，显然拆不开别人机房里的那一半。 另外，工具多也未必是好事。Duncan Ogilvie 说过，他不认为给模型暴露更多工具能让它表现更好；现在也确实已经有 REA 用户抱怨，它塞给智能体的工具说明太长，用不了多久就把上下文挤满了。 REA 真正新的地方，其实在还是在被大幅降低的逆向门槛 。 以前想让 AI 帮你逆向，你得先是个会逆向的人：装好 IDA，配好插件，知道该问什么。现在一行 npx rea-agents setup，选好要接入的智能体、点头确认，配置就写好了。把它推上热榜的，也不是安全圈，是 AI 博主和科技大号。 REA 的技术不新，新的是用它的人。 「逆向」AI 做，「牢」用户坐 新用户带来的第一个问题，就藏在那句宣传语里：给你的项目里加上类似功能。拆开来看，和照着做一个，在法律上是两件事。 拆一个软件，法律上大致要过三个层面： 商业秘密、版权，还有合同 。 首先是商业机密，最高人民法院 2020 年关于商业秘密案件的司法解释写得很明白：对从公开渠道取得的产品做拆卸、测绘、分析，拿到技术信息，不算侵犯商业秘密。前提是东西来路正，先用不正当手段拿到秘密、再拿逆向当说辞，法院不认。 版权这部分，《计算机软件保护条例》第十七条允许为了学习和研究软件里的设计思想和原理去使用软件，2020 年修正的《著作权法》第五十条，把「计算机软件反向工程研究」列为可以避开技术措施的情形之一。 但大多数商业软件的用户协议里，都有一条禁止反编译的条款。在美国这一条是经常被引用且能执行的：2003 年的 Bowers 诉 Baystate 案里，联邦巡回上诉法院认定，软件许可里的禁止逆向条款有效，逆向之后做出竞品的一方，按违约赔了钱。 欧盟反过来，合同里禁止为互操作而反编译的条款，一律无效。同一件事，换个地方答案就不同。 《著作权法》第五十条：豁免的是「研究」｜图片来源：中国政府网 至于照着做一个，这里其实有个好消息：版权保护的是代码怎么写，不保护功能本身。条例第六条写得清楚，保护不延及开发软件所用的思想、处理过程和操作方法。单从版权看，别人有个好用的搜索功能，你自己写一个效果相似的，本身不违法。 麻烦其实出在它是怎么写出来的。软件行业应对这件事有一套老办法，叫 净室开发：一组人去拆对方的产品，只写出功能说明书；另一组从没看过对方代码的人，照着说明书从头写。 两组之间隔着一道墙，墙就是日后打官司时的证据，证明新代码是独立写出来的。 REA 现在把这道墙拆了：读反编译结果的是这个智能体，写新代码的还是这个智能体，中间没有任何隔断。Hacker News 上有人把这种做法叫作「洗知识产权」；一个复刻 Photoshop 的项目，开发者说他们团队明确禁止成员用 Ghidra 和 REA，原因很简单，怕被起诉。 游戏圈把这件事推到了极端。Maurice 那种做法叫字节级匹配反编译：写出来的源码，编译之后要和原程序一个字节都不差，他说这给了智能体一个非对即错的客观信号。净室追求的是「我没照着你写」，字节级匹配追求的恰恰是「写得和你一模一样」。 发行商的反应也很直接。 10

title: 尊界：11 月起陆续升级踏板；iPhone 折叠屏国内预约超 200 万；6 个月，超千万 Claude 账户被封杀｜极客早知道
summary: 陶哲轩提出「数学 2.0」：AI 解题之外，还要帮助人理解证明 10 月 11 日，数学家陶哲轩公开了在加州理工学院的演讲《数学 2.0》。他认为，AI 正在降低部分数学问题的求解成本，使数学研究逐渐从「证明稀缺」走向「证明富足」。但目前多数前沿问题仍未解决，不能只凭公开传播的成功案例判断 AI 的整体能力。 陶哲轩指出，得到正确证明，并不意味着研究者理解了证明为何成立，或掌握了可用于其他问题的新方法。他主张用 AI 寻找更易理解的证明、整理分散的研究成果，并对大量数学问题开展系统分析。例如，等式理论项目通过人类与自动化工具协作，对超过 2200 万个命题作出了判定。 对于 AI 解题能力的评估，他还呼吁公开计算资源消耗、失败尝试等信息。在陶哲轩看来，未来数学研究既要利用 AI 扩展探索范围，也要保留人类对证明及其现实应用的理解和判断。（来源：机器之心） Claude 爆发大规模封号潮：半年封杀 1140 万个账号申诉后仅 4.2 万翻案 10 月 11 日，据媒体报道，近期 Claude 账号封禁问题引发开发者讨论。受到关注的一项数据来自 Anthropic 今年 7 月发布的报告：2026 年上半年，平台累计封禁约 1140 万个账号；收到约 39.8 万次申诉，其中约 4.2 万次申诉成功。报告未披露完整的封禁原因分布，仅凭这些数字也无法判断近期封号是否增加，但申诉结果使平台的封禁标准和复核机制受到关注。 Anthropic 列出的违规情形包括利用服务从事违法活动、侵犯隐私，以及违反地区使用限制等。今年上半年，Anthropic 还向相关儿童安全组织提交了超过 1.5 万起报告。 此外，Anthropic 近期修订了 Claude 使用政策，计划自 11 月 12 日起禁止用户在没有明显目的的情况下，反复对模型实施极端残忍行为。公司称，新规针对的是极端情形；用户表达不满、反驳模型、创作黑暗题材内容，以及开展模型测试与研究，不属于该项禁令的范围。（来源：快科技） 英伟达洽谈收购 Reflection AI，已投资 8 亿美元，后者估值达 250 亿美元 10 月 11 日，据媒体报道，英伟达正与美国人工智能初创企业 Reflection AI 就潜在收购或进一步扩大投资展开初步谈判，交易可能采取全面收购、追加股权投资、提供更多芯片及算力支持，或通过聘用员工并获得技术授权等多种形式。英伟达此前已向 Reflection AI 投资 8 亿美元，是其最大股东之一。 知情人士透露，双方可能在未来数周内达成协议。Reflection AI 今年 3 月融资时的估值达到 250 亿美元，其开发的开放权重 AI 模型被美国政府视为抗衡 DeepSeek 等低成本竞争对手的重要技术资源。（来源：新浪科技） 消息称 OLED 屏新款 iPad mini 售价将大幅上涨，或接近 799 美元 10 月 11 日，彭博社记者马克 · 古尔曼表示，苹果计划本月晚些时候推出新款 iPad mini。新机的起步存储空间可能会有所提升，但有意换机的用户得提前做好涨价的准备。 古尔曼透露，新款 iPad mini 售价相比现款机型将大幅上涨，预计将接近 799 美元（IT 之家注：现汇率约合 5,359 元人民币）。作为对比，现款 iPad mini 7 价格为 599 美元（现汇率约合 4,017 元人民币）/4,799 元人民币。 据悉，新款 iPad mini 将首次采用 OLED 屏幕，配备重新设计的机身。预计将拥有全新扬声器系统，搭载性能更强的芯片。（来源：IT 之家） 京东预约超 200 万人：苹果 iPhone Duo 折叠屏手机 15999 元起倒数 5 天预售 10 月 11 日，iPhone Duo 定价 15999 元起，国行 10 月 16 日晚 8 点接受预购。 京东目前预约人数已超 200 万人，需要注意的是： iPhone Duo 仅支持 eSIM 京东渠道首批可能需要签收激活（以下单时宝贝标题 / 咨询客服为准，就算不用任何补贴，也需激活后才能签收）（来源：IT 之家） 尊界：踏板升级方案预计于 10 月底确认，11 月起陆续启动升级 10 月 11 日下午，尊界客服向记者确认，尊界 V800 制动踏板支架底座升级方案预计于 10 月底确认，11 月起陆续启动升级。 10 月 8 日晚，尊界汽车发布关于尊界汽车制动踏板支架底座相关问题的情况说明，称将进一步优化该部件设计，并为已交付用户提供免费升级选择。 11 日下午，尊界客服告诉记者，目前，已提车的用户可通过全国任一服务中心预约登记，也可直接联系购车门店登记，届时用户中心将会第一时间联系用户；而未发运车辆会被直接升级后再交付，用户无需额外操作。（来源： 北京日报 ） 比亚迪李柯：五年内赶超丰田、大众 登顶全球车企销量第一 10 月 11 日，日前，比亚迪执行副总裁、国际业务负责人李柯在新加坡一场峰会上明确了公司下一阶段的全球战略目标，计划未来五年内赶超丰田和大众，成为全球最大汽车制造商。她表示，比亚迪将坚持出海战略，持续开拓欧洲、中美洲、南美洲、亚洲和大洋洲市场，并强调公司在储能、光伏、电池等多个领域实现领跑，电池技术是核心竞争力之一，优势不只在汽车。 谈到美国市场，李柯明确表示暂时不进入，原因是美国拟以立法形式强化对中国相关联网汽车及车辆软件进入美国市场的限制，即便在美国设厂的极星，也不得不转向其他市场销售。（来源：cnBeta） SpaceXAI 官方账号更名为 SpaceX Super Intelligence 10 月 11 日，马斯克当地时间

title: 12 分钟订单破万，吉利银河战舰 700，要订下新能源越野的新标准
summary: 图片来源：吉利银河 「这台车我们造了 5 年，这也是吉利第一次造越野车。」吉利汽车研究院院长李传海说到。 就在几分钟前，10 月 10 日，吉利银河战舰 700，一台新能源野车正式发布，16.98 万（限时焕新价）起的价格，让这台最高配备三电机四驱，千匹马力，能爬 45° 坡、能应急浮水的越野车，变得十分打动人心。 吉利银河战舰 700 的价格梯度比较大｜图片来源：极客公园 事实也是如此，在发布会后 12 分钟，吉利银河战舰 700 的订单数量就突破 1 万台。 但在显性成功的背后，你确实会猜测，可能恰恰因为吉利「缺乏越野基因」，才能让团队没有任何包袱，从底层架构层面，重新思考新能源时代的越野车，到底应该是什么样。或者， 用吉利团队的话，是新能源越野时代 2.0 的产品，该是怎样的 ？ 大梁，「吃」进车里 过去十几年，硬派越野车的规矩很简单。想要真越野，就上非承载式大梁，车身坐在一副独立的钢制梯形车架上，扛得住扭，经得起摔，代价是车重、空间被吃掉、进城开起来晃晃悠悠。想要舒适，就选承载式车身，好开好坐，但遇到交叉轴和连续冲击，车身容易扭，严重时车门都关不严。 新能源来了之后，这道题反而更难。电池要找地方放，电机要找地方装，大梁车本来就紧张的底盘空间被进一步压缩，车重再往上叠几百公斤。市面上不少新能源硬派，其实是在两条老路里选一条走，要么在大梁车上做加法，要么给城市 SUV 套一个方盒子外壳。 银河战舰 700 的思路，是不再二选一。 吉利集团 CEO 淦家阅介绍 GTA 架构和一体大梁技术｜图片来源：极客公园 它基于吉利新发布的 GTA 原生新能源越野架构， 核心是一套被称为「一体式大梁」的结构 。简单理解，就是把大梁拆成三段分别用最合适的工艺来做，再整体嵌进车身骨架。前纵梁用超高强热成形钢，中段是超高强辊压集成大梁，后纵梁用 TRB 热成形（一种变厚度轧制工艺，受力大的地方厚，受力小的地方薄），三段前后贯通，再和门槛梁、横梁连成一个整体。 这么做的收益体现在几组数字上。官方数据显示，这套结构的强度比传统大梁提升 30% 以上，整车扭转刚度做到 44180 N·m/deg，比同级独立大梁车型高出 20% 以上。与此同时，它比独立大梁方案轻 80 到 100 公斤，高度方向省出 40 到 70 毫米，换来更大的头部空间和 80.3% 的得房率。 它想要大梁车的「骨头」，又不想背大梁车的「包袱」。 需要说清楚的是，从结构分类上看，这依然是一台承载式车身的车，吉利早期资料里也用过「内嵌式梯形半承载」的说法。它并不是传统意义上的非承载大梁车，这套结构在长期高强度越野中的可靠性，最终还要交给时间和用户来检验。 吉利银河战舰 700 的底盘｜图片来源：极客公园 架构只是起点。新能源越野之所以值得从头设计，还因为电机能做到传统机械四驱做不到的事。 银河战舰 700 的雷神 EM-T 采用三电机布局，前面是发动机加三挡 DHT 电驱，后桥是两台独立的轮边电机，单台峰值功率 220kW。两台后电机各自控制左右车轮的扭矩，再加上前后轴之间的扭矩分配，就构成了两把随时待命的「智能软锁」；后桥另有一把电控机械差速锁，0.2 秒内完成 100% 锁止。这就是吉利所说的「两软一硬」。 专门为吉利银河战舰打造的 EM-T 混动技术｜图片来源：极客公园 传统越野车的机械锁，往往要等车轮打滑之后才介入，或者需要驾驶者提前判断、手动开启。 三电机的逻辑是在打滑发生之前，就把扭矩送到有附着力的车轮上 。顶配 2.0T 车型系统综合功率 830kW，合 1129 匹马力，在巴丹吉林沙漠的尼三锅沙山上，满载五人、零速起步、不助跑，一把直拔登顶。 底盘同样是一套为城野两头准备的组合。前双叉臂加前悬 6 点硬连接，2.0T 车型后悬也换成双叉臂，悬架行程 280mm；双腔闭式空簧负责高度和刚度，有 120mm 的升降行程，城市里降低，越野时抬高；CCD 连续可变阻尼减振器每秒调节 500 次。官方给出的麋鹿测试成绩是公路 80km/h，沙地 72.1km/h。 安全是这套架构的另一半。在一体式大梁之外，银河战舰 700 用 11 根 2200MPa 的热气胀管做了一个隐藏式防滚架，覆盖 A、B、C、D 柱、上边梁和后顶横梁，总长 10.6 米，整车顶压 161kN。李传海在群访中换算过，这大约是 16 吨，相当于整车重量的 5 倍多。电池包则做了内凹设计，底部离地 313mm，比整车最低点高出 80 毫米。 他还讲了一个细节。工程师曾在沙漠坡道上刻意把车掀翻，别的车可能要滚好几圈，而这台车翻过来一圈就停住了。原因是开发时反复推敲车宽、轮胎宽度和质心高度， 目标是先让车尽量不翻，翻了也要保住乘员舱。 这些设计背后是同一个判断，新能源越野车不是给燃油越野车「插上电」，而是要从结构开始重做一遍。 越野很酷，但大部分时间在城里 一个不太浪漫的事实是，买硬派 SUV 的人，绝大多数时间都在城里开。 吉利银河销售公司常务副总经理关久旸在群访中提到，有一类用户更在意好看的外观和时尚的内饰，驾驶场景 98% 都在城区。研发负责人的表述更直接，这台车首先要解决用户 80% 到 90% 的日常通勤，「就像一个真正的大五座 SUV」。 所以， 银河战舰 700 的智能化，首先是为城市准备的 。 高配车型搭载千里浩瀚 H7 方案，使用 Thor-U 芯片，算力 700TOPS，配备激光雷达和 29 个感知硬件，支持 D2D 车位到车位的领航辅助。从驶出车位、出入地库、通过闸机，到高速和城区 NOA，再到泊入目标车位，全程不需要人为衔接。泊车覆盖 300 多种车位类型，包括断头路车位、机械车位和极窄车位，还支持离车泊入和手机遥控的「指尖泊车」。 对一台 5 米多长、近 2 米宽的方盒子来说，这些功能的价值远比在一台普通轿车上大。 吉利银河战舰 700 的内饰设计也有很多巧思｜图片来源：极客公园 静谧性也是重点照顾的部分。路噪主动降噪、发动机主动降噪、前后排双层夹胶玻璃叠加之后，官方数据是 120km/h 时车内噪声 68.4 分贝。 title: Quoting Geoffrey Huntley
summary: If the agent isn't using my diagnostics library, I could introspect and update AGENTS.md, but there's still a delta, and it'll drift. Instead, I write a pre-commit hook that checks the git diff for direct calls to observability modules that bypass my diagnostics module. Boom: fail the commit, inject a prompt telling the agent to use the diagnostics library. All of a sudden it's ten out of ten. — Geoffrey Huntley , nobody should type code by hand anymore. here's what's left. title: Less scrolling, more living: How Whimscope is turning everyday ideas into adventures
summary: People often want to do more interesting things but struggle to decide what to do, find the energy to organise something, or commit to a big activity. Consumer app Whimscope aims to remove that struggle by helping people break out of their everyday routines through small, achievable adventures based on their available time, energy, and mood. Think of it as a combination of an activity discovery app, a bucket list, and a gentle nudge to do something different. Whimscope follows a three-stage process: Dream, Plan, Do. Users discover activities and experiences, choose something to try immediately or save for later, and record their completed adventures through photos, notes, and memories. These activities, known as whims, range from small everyday experiences to more ambitious adventures, such as trying a new hobby, visiting a local attraction, learning to surf, taking a spontaneous trip to a lighthouse, or planning a memorable day out with family. Some take just 15 minutes, while others might fill an evening or an entire weekend, and can be enjoyed alone or with others. title: CarbonFarm raises €7M to tackle methane emissions from rice cultivation
summary: CarbonFarm , a digital monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) provider specialising in rice decarbonisation, has raised €7 million in an oversubscribed Series A funding round to expand its technology and support projects worldwide. The round was led by Colam Impact , with participation from Proparco, Suma Capital, elea, Working Capital Fund, Albo and Bpifrance. Existing investors Serena and makesense, through Racine², and Techmind also participated. CarbonFarm develops technology and provides project development services to help the rice industry reduce greenhouse gas emissions, improve water management and access climate finance. The company works with rice producers, cooperatives, agribusinesses, NGOs, governments and local project developers to implement and measure changes in farming practices. Rice cultivation accounts for around 12 per cent of human-caused methane emissions globally and uses up to 28 per cent of the world's freshwater resources. Improved water management can reduce emissions by up to 50 per cent and water use by 30 per cent without affecting yields. However, implementing these practices at scale remains challenging, as rice farming is dominated by smallholders, requiring coordination across thousands of farms and reliable methods to measure environmental impact. title: Monopulse raises over €2M to advance electronic warfare-resistant drones
summary: Danish-Lithuanian Unmanned aerial vehicle manufacturer MNP Technologijos, operating under the Monopulse brand, has raised over €2 million from investors in Lithuania and abroad. Investors included Coinvest Capital, Plug and Play, LitBAN, and NGL Ventures, whose angel syndicate contributed €560,000 from 68 investors, its largest syndicate to date. Founded in 2021, Monopulse develops advanced reconnaissance drones for NATO militaries, and its technology covers both aerial and water-based surveillance. Its technology focuses on making drones more reliable in electronic warfare environments, where communications and navigation signals can be disrupted or jammed. Monopulse combines aerospace engineering, electronics, sensor fusion, computer vision, and AI to develop drones capable of maintaining communications or operating autonomously when signals are lost. Its products include the Falcon MK3S drone platform, with variants for intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance, and other specialist applications, alongside the Hydrohex system. The company has 14 team members, including engineers, researchers, and former military personnel, and develops its core hardware and software capabilities in-house. summary: Scarlet , the certification body for AI and software medical devices, today announced a $50 million Series B led by Headline , with participation from new investor Notion Capital and existing investors Atomico, Creandum, Kindred Capital, and Entrepreneurs First. Nancy Xiao Mclaughlin, Partner at Headline, joins Scarlet’s board. AI medical devices are being developed faster than certification bodies can review them. A company can train an AI diagnostic model in weeks and then wait 12 to 18 months for an assessment by experts, with another six to eight months of unnecessary delay for approval of a minor update, slowing down healthcare innovation. Scarlet is a government-designated certification body. summary: The UK AI minister today called on frontier AI labs to ramp up the safety of their leading AI systems, as the UK announced it was strengthening its cyber defences, including potential new legislation, as it prepares for potential serious AI incidents. Investigate unexpected behaviour. Narayan today said Britain must act now to strengthen its defences and prepare for future serious incidents as AI frontier models become increasingly powerful and capable of acting autonomously. summary: German energytech unicorn 1KOMMA5° has reached a valuation of $1.35 billion in its latest financing round as it prepares to increase investment in its AI-powered energy management business. If you're interested in reading how they got started, published over 6 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. Hey! I am Matti Lehtonen, MD of Backstage Rock Shop Ltd . We do merchandise for music acts, mainly in the rock and metal scene and we are based in Tampere, Finland. We handle the official webshops for around 50 bands and e-commerce is our core business but we do also sell items live in concerts, tours, and festivals. In normal situations, we do 200 - 300 live shows annually, now in covid time unfortunately a lot less. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? It’s been quite an interesting year due to all covid related things. E-commerce has been growing and last year (2020) we shipped well over 50,000 online store orders, this year we’ve been sending pretty much the same amount of packages as last year. We’ve done more marketing and many new marketing co-operations are starting this fall so looking good in that sector. Learn what others in your business are doing, always be on top of things so that you know what is going on in your industry. Live business, on the other hand, selling band merchandise at festivals, tours, and concerts have been pretty quiet. I mean we had some kind of festival summer here in Finland this year but all the major festivals were canceled as well as all happenings earlier this year so for us, it has meant that in the live sector we’ve lost quite a lot of revenue. But next year will be the biggest so far for sure. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? Things might take more time. Production times with some items and factories are growing because of covid, also delivery costs globally. Even though merchandise and especially textiles are our core items, we also release music. With the vinyl boom during the past few years, the production times have been ridiculous. In early 2021 we were talking about 6-7 weeks of production, in August 2021 we are talking about 5-6 months so you need to plan things well ahead. Also, one thing that has changed this year is that things do change with really short notice so you need to react faster than before. What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? This fall we are celebrating our 10th anniversary and we are also moving to bigger premises in late September. Our current premises are 475m2 and the new one will be over 800m2 of just renovated space which we have planned ourselves so we are looking forward to this. The new premises will make operations a lot more efficient. We also have a lot of new cool releases and launches coming later this year and during the next year so 2022 will be our best year so far for sure. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? Learn what others in your business are doing, and always be on top of things so that you know what is going on in your industry. Talk with other companies in your industry. At least here in Finland in our business, we do a lot of cooperation with other companies in our industry. Even though they are our competitors, there are always win-win situations that you can get with other companies. Do not be afraid of failure, try new things. If you don’t try, you won’t achieve anything. Where can we go to learn more? Website Facebook If you have any questions or comments, drop a comment below! Grant Cardone The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck: A Counterintuitive A... Mark Manson Want more updates on Rockstar Mind? Check out these stories: Hello! Who are you and what business did you start? My name is Steve Mastroianni and I am the owner of Rockstar Mind Inc. , which is an online coaching platform. I’ve focused on coaching guitarists and songwriters, and most recently have been doing business coaching under my HOBBY BOSS brand. Some of the main products I sell are private coaching and interactive workshops. I’m also the author of two best-selling books. My main customers are typically musicians, like myself, who want to improve their ability to play songs faster, write their own songs, and perform them live. The business generates six figures per year serving hundreds of customers per month and it’s all run by me and my team of 3 virtual assistants. What s your backstory and how did you come up with the idea? So I’ve been a professional musician for over 15 years. One of the highlights of my career was getting signed to a record deal by Gene Simmons and touring North America opening for KISS. That experience was really like a masterclass in marketing on how to develop and nurture a solid fan base. While making plans with my band for our next album, I got a phone call from my father telling me that he was just diagnosed with Stage IV Colon Cancer. That call instantly changed my life; I went from being a rockstar to a caregiver and decided to put my budding music career on hold to help look after my father. During that time I needed to find a creative way to pay my rent while still having the flexibility to be there for my father. I was also in about $20,000 in debt, so I knew that whatever option I pursued had to be viable for my future financial goals. Be okay with failing multiple times to succeed. A big part of making it as an entrepreneur is knowing how to bounce back after each loss and trying every approach until you find a way to make it work. It was actually one of my guitar students that suggested I start a guitar website and teach online. I brushed it off at first since there are so many guitar sites online, but I kept getting more and more requests from my fans and students so I decided to go for it. Soon afterward, Rockstar Mind was born one afternoon while I was at the hospital with my father. At the time Rockstar Mind was born (in 2014), I just needed enough to pay the bills and a little extra for some fun money. It wasn’t until my first daughter was born in 2018 that I knew I needed to start taking my business more seriously so that I could provide for my family and have more financial stability. Take us through the process of designing the initial product. By the time I started Rockstar Mind, I had already been coaching for over 10 years. I had a strong client base to start my business; I was really familiar with who they were, their needs, and their goals. From there it was a matter of finding more customers who were like them. Be okay with the risks, and there will be many; that’s why starting and running your own business is one of the most exhilarating things you can do. Remember that the risks you take and the hard work you put in will often pay out the highest reward. When thinking of my ideal customer, I went into extreme detail based on my past and current students and my knowledge of the market. I filled in any blanks by researching forums, joining Facebook groups to better understand who they were. All of my marketing research was digital, and as a result, I found a lot of people with large audiences and made some relationships with them. Because of our relationship, they were willing to promote my business to their audience. For example, I connected with JB Partners and had them promote Rockstar Mind to their email lists. I gave 100% commissions on the first product (a guitar course), and then I kept all the commission for any memberships purchased on the back end. Startup costs ended up being really low for me - I recorded courses on my phone and may be paid around $200 for a website domain and video hosting fees. Describe the process of launching the business. Preparing to launch Rockstar Mind was fairly simple. I bought some WordPress plugins, video editing software, web hosting, website domain name registration, and a new webcam. Keep in mind that nothing I bought for the business was fancy, and I used credit cards to purchase all of it. Beyond that, I used whatever I had around my house. I mentioned earlier that I lined up a lot of affiliate promotions, and that was what I used to launch Rockstar Mind. My affiliates sent promotions to their audience, I promoted to my fans on social media and my small emailing list. I had friends promoting on their social media channels, and I even promoted on my band’s fan page as well. Systematize as much as you can early in the game so you can more easily outsource the small jobs. The goal is for you to work on the business and not in the business as much as possible. Because Rockstar Mind is an online business, a lot of the work happened on the back end to prepare for the launch so when launch day came, it was almost as simple as flipping a switch. Like I said earlier, Rockstar Mind was born while I was at the hospital with my dad; on May 11, 2014, at 2:34 pm to be exact. What I learned from launching Rockstar Mind is that everything that you want to do for your launch is going to take about 3x longer and is about 3x harder than you originally think it’s going to be. You really have to do whatever you can to stand out because there’s a lot of noise online. So whether that’s to your clientele or the business partners you’re trying to develop solid relationships with. It’s really all about relationships, both with customers and with your business partners. Since launch, what has worked to attract and retain customers? I’ve had the best results in my business from following the principles of direct response marketing. Direct response states that 60% of your success comes from promoting to the right people, and to do that you have to know where they are and how to capture their attention. I’m a big believer in paid advertising on social media platforms. My personal favorites are Facebook and Amazon (but I also think YouTube and Google are also great and viable options). What appealed to me was their lower entry point. I would run ads for a while, and once I knew I had a winning ad I would increase my budget. You’ll naturally garner interest through advertising, but having and growing an email list is imperative to growing your business. I’m careful to always point any potential customers to my email list because it provides me a way to keep in touch with them. I’m quick to respond to any emails that come in through social media or my website - I believe that relationship nurturing has done a lot to build my business. Keep in mind that my email lists weren’t always large. In 2019, my email list only had 3,000 people on it, and yet in that same year, I grew my business from $0 to over $100,000. How are you doing today and what does the future look like? Today, Rockstar Mind is a six-figure business and I’m planning on growing it to a seven-figure business in the coming year or two. I’ve launched two best-selling books and am now coaching others on how to start and grow their businesses while still running the guitar coaching side so I can keep sharp. Designed by my co-founder and partner, Jon, who is an architect by trade, as he became aspirated with how much paper he was wasting printing draft designs that quickly became obsolete, he created a simple notebook with the paper, writing notes on the perfectly pristine back blank sides of his designs. Drawing attention whenever he brought out his self-made eco-friendly notebook, it gradually became a sustainable business idea; the Paper Saver aims to promote environmental awareness and sustainable living by demonstrating how easy it is to reduce waste in everyday tasks. The Paper Saver repurposes your paper as pages of its notebook, reducing paper waste and helping the environment. Encasing a functionally designed spring steel binder inside, your discarded paper is inserted and folded so you can conveniently write on the back blank sides - no more unnecessary new notebooks as you will have an endless supply of used paper as pages of your Paper Saver! Available in three different designs - the Classic Paper Saver (made of faux leather), the Leather Paper Saver (made of genuine leather), and the Sparkle Paper Saver (made of canvas). Since launching in 2015, we have grown YOY on an average of 30%. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? Covid-19 has impacted our business as events have played a large part in our marketing calendar and sales. 2020 was the year that we had locked in even more events than usual, but everything was obviously either canceled or postponed. Marketing budgets were cut across many businesses, which impacted us as corporate orders for customized Paper Savers contribute to a large part of our sales as well. Hence we focused our energies on paid social media advertising, creating new ads that were tailored to the ‘new norm’ of consumers working from home, much managing online learning, and of course - printing! There is never a right or wrong, but only an opportunity to try or not try. If you try and find out it wasn’t right, take it as a learning, not a failure. It is simply an issue of your mindset in how you define success. There was uncertainty like there had been for any business at the beginning of Covid-19, about how marketing messages would be viewed and accepted. So it was a trial first with a small budget, and ensuring we were targeting our audience as best as we could - and what happened? It delivered well over 300% in ROI. So this was a great win for us, and through 2020, it continued this way - trial and error until we saw the successful returns. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? One lesson learned from last year was, off the success of our paid social media campaign as per the above, we let it keep running without refreshing it for a while - this was a mistake as, after a while, it wore off. Facebook likes to see fresh campaigns, and so the success almost scared us from doing what we knew should have been done - to keep the ads fresh. We also utilized the downtime to finally make a bigger dent in the US market by tapping into the Amazon network. Many people around us had been telling us that we need to get onto Amazon US, but it never made the top of our priority list. Shipping costs from Australia to the US always hindered our customers from purchasing from our website, so now that Amazon US ships directly for us, it has been great so far! 2020 also was a year of change for us at Paper Saver, as I decided to return to a corporate job while continuing to maintain Paper Saver as a side business. Times in lockdown make you evaluate everything in your life and I came to the conclusion that I wanted to put my energies into helping make more of a difference in the world and contributing to social good, and so I have moved into the for-purpose space :) Paper Saver is continuing to run, as we still have a distributor managing our wholesale business in Australia, online and custom orders are still managed by my partner; I just have less time obviously to manage the marketing side of things, but we are still active and running! What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? In the short term, we would love to see the return of our local events - design markets and events that we had signed up for in 2019 are all due to happen later this year. It is going to be super exciting just to be face-to-face with our consumers again! Many of our events made an online version, which we also supported - as we are all small businesses supporting each other, we have wanted to continue the relationship with these event organizers. We are planning several different, new initiatives in how we execute our events this year. There are also plans to update the Leather Paper Saver. There are ways we can refresh the design, the card and document pockets inside, and even the material itself as we would love to source an even more sustainable option so that we continue to walk our sustainable talk. Watch this space! On a more long-term scale, we would love to continue to expand more into the US market - Amazon has shown us that there is room to grow there. As we return more to a pre-Covid life, we would love to become involved in the trade shows in the US and enlist stockists for the Paper Saver in the US market. As mentioned, shipping costs have always hindered our customers in North America, so this would make a bigger difference in our US sales. Have you read any good books in the last year? Thrive: The Third Metric to Redefining Success and Creating a Life of Well-Being , Wisdom and Wonder , by Arianna Huffington. This was a good read for me as a mum and wife, a business owner, and my decision to return to corporate work. If anyone is in a similar position, juggling the many tasks of numerous roles and hats, this affirms for you that you just need to find the right balance as your measure of success. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? My partner had wanted to start the Paper Saver for a few years and I had been the one pushing back. In the end, he became so determined he had completed designs and had started sourcing suppliers. I saw through his determination and gave in, concluding that the worst-case scenario would be that we would have 500 Paper Savers sitting around (the minimum order quantity from the supplier he found, who is still our supplier today) and a few thousand dollars down the drain. To date, I can proudly say that we turned around a profit from day one and the Paper Saver continues to be a great side hustle for us! There is never a right or wrong, but only an opportunity to try or not try. If you try and find out it wasn’t right, take it as a learning, not a failure. It is simply an issue of your mindset in how you define success. Where can we go to learn more? Website Facebook Instagram If you have any questions or comments, drop a comment below! Switching Careers And Starting My Own Digital Marketing Agency (2019) ➜ This is a follow up story for Smart Yeti. If you're interested in reading how they got started, published over 7 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. My name is Jeremy Kanne, and I am the owner/founder of Smart Yeti . Smart Yeti provides Fractional Chief Marketing Officer services to B2B Tech/SaaS companies. The journey here has been a long but good one. I started Smart Yeti with the approach of finding the best-fit video production services in a market that didn’t want to provide middle-cost options because it’s hard. Within a few years, I expanded Smart Yeti’s scope to include most brand deliverables - websites, design, brand, etc. with the same philosophy of finding the best fit service according to need and budget. We target businesses making $1-15 million annually and are B2B businesses - particularly technology and software / SaaS companies. Typically, the pain points seen in our target customer base are that they’ve “tried marketing” but haven’t seen the results they desired or are struggling to find the most cost-efficient solution. We come in with a practiced hand across multiple marketing strategies and help hire fire agencies, revise strategy to fit business goals, and assist in managing execution to eliminate roadblocks. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? Smart Yeti’s journey in marketing has taken another turn. We started as a video production agency and then expanded into a creative agency. Now we are in what I expect to be the final pivot - providing Fractional Chief Marketing Officer services. I’m proud of this change in direction because it meets all the goals I want to see in being an exceptional partner in marketing. I saw an opportunity to leverage the problem-solving skills forged in my engineering background to provide valuable ongoing marketing support. Through all the iterations I’ve taken Smart Yeti through, I’ve always been focused on providing the best fit solution to their marketing needs - first in the video, then across all creative, and now in marketing strategy and systems. This move felt right because in previously providing video or design or website needs, this was only a part of the larger problem. I often felt like I was making a great asset that the client was pleased with, but we wouldn’t know what results it helped achieve in the larger marketing strategy. This is often because the client did not have a larger marketing strategy or didn’t know how to best utilize the work in their strategy. This realization led me to work with clients on strategy. But I wasn’t satisfied with just creating another marketing agency that focuses on a handful of strategies/tactics. Companies have ongoing marketing needs that change as the marketing landscape changes or tactics prove less than effective. I saw an opportunity to leverage the problem-solving skills forged in my engineering background to provide valuable ongoing marketing support. Fractional Chief Marketing Officer services proved to be the best way to be the trusted marketing strategist for clients that I wanted to be and it has proven to be a great decision. With our largest client, we were happy to report a 56% increase in lead activity compared to previous years before our Smart Yeti engagement and the client has shared that they feel like using a fractional Chief Marketing Officer was “the best marketing decision they’ve ever made.” Hearing that, I couldn’t be happier. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? I’ve learned that there is a serious issue with conflict-free advice when it comes to marketing strategy. Marketing agencies, typically working on a specific set of tactics/methods often sell themselves as doing “marketing strategy” while simultaneously recommending their services within their recommended strategy. I don’t see a fault in them doing this, but it leaves the responsibility up to the client to judge their strategic recommendations accordingly, and all too often, small-to-medium business CEOs don’t have the marketing expertise to make a truly informed choice. What results is companies trying out various agencies and tactics without a long-term plan in place, directly leading to feelings of ‘throwing spaghetti against the wall’ or ‘marketing just doesn’t work for us.’ Be open, honest, and vulnerable. Treat every piece of feedback with respect and try to learn at least a little from it. And then the more feedback you get, the easier you’ll be able to find insightful patterns. In my marketing career, I’ve long been searching for an honest way to bring value to companies without championing a certain strategy or tactic. This was for two big reasons: Any given strategy may need to be revised in the future as the market and needs shift. Any given strategy may or may not be the right fit for a company and I despise trying to sell something that isn’t valuable to a person. Shifting into being a Fractional Chief Marketing Officer has been a great fit for my skills because I get to give strategic, uncompromised advice that puts the client’s business goals at the highest priority. What’s in the plans for the upcoming year and the next 5 years? Short-term plans (the next 1-2 years) are to gather data on this new Fractional MCO model and make a decision on whether to expand internal capabilities. If I decide to expand, that will mean slowly bringing on new Fractional CMOS. Any good onboarding/training needs careful consideration, implementation, and feedback. Have you read any good books in the last year? Highly highly recommend Ministry For The Future . It’s a near-future sci-fi novel that is both entertaining and terrifying, looking at what might happen given our world’s current course about climate change. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? Get. Feedback. You’ll be in the best place to expand when you know exactly what problem you’re trying to solve and who the solution works best for. The best way I know to know this is to ask questions during and after the sales process. Be open, honest, and vulnerable. Treat every piece of feedback with respect and try to learn at least a little from it. And then the more feedback you get, the easier you’ll be able to find insightful patterns. If you're interested in reading how they got started, published over 6 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. We are Drs. Jenna and Travis Zigler, and we are the founders of Eye Love and Heyedrate, which we started in 2015. Our main goal is to help 1,000,000 people suffering from dry, irritated eyes, and we’re well on our way to doing this through our line of eye health products. Six years ago, we started Eye Love with the simple goal of giving us a little extra cash to go on eye care mission trips. Within a few years, Eye Love has become more than we ever could have imagined. Our main product is Heyedrate Lid and Lash Cleanser, which helps keep your eyelids clean and healthy. This hypochlorous acid cleanser is so important because excess bacteria on the eyelids often lead to dry, irritated eyes. Without healthy eyelids, you wouldn’t have comfortable eyes and clear vision. Eye Love has grown immensely in the past few years, and we’re now regularly doing $400,000 per month. Eye Love was acquired on June 2, 2021, by Physician Recommended Nutriceuticals (PRN), and we can’t wait to see how the synergy is going to play out in the next few years. We’ll both be staying on to continue to run Eye Love with our current team for the next few years, and this is exactly what we wanted from a sale. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? I mentioned earlier that we sold our business in June of this year, and this would not have been possible without exploring new avenues of marketing and increasing our product offerings. In May of 2020, we acquired a business, MediViz, which sells similar products to ours but also gave us a few products that helped to round out our offerings. More specifically, MediViz was a great buy for us because we knew the owner personally, teamed up with him, and were able to bring more products into our ecosystem while decreasing the amount of money they were spending on duplicate software and services. By bringing MediViz into Eye Love, it allowed us to grow incredibly well in 2020 despite everything going on in the world. What we realized in 2020 was that getting from $0 to $1 million is the hardest part of the business. This is where you are learning how to sell, who to serve, and how to do it all. Going from $1 to $10 million is all about releasing more products, which is what we are focusing on now more than ever. Getting to $10 million is our 3-year goal. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? In the past few years, we’ve learned the importance of focusing on what we do best. We know Amazon through and through, yet we spent way too much time and money trying to build out our website. The minute we quit focusing on our website and focused back on Amazon, we began to see much higher sales off Amazon! Look for how you can serve others, and your business is much more likely to take off than if you’re constantly focused on the money. All eyes are on Amazon and the majority of people are buying there. The great thing is, many of these people would rather purchase directly from us so we’ve seen an increase in website traffic by simply growing our Amazon presence. What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? We have plans to release a new eye cream and face moisturizer that contains no toxic preservatives like phenoxyethanol, which is in all “organic” face creams. It also doesn’t contain retinol which can be great for anti-aging, but it’s terrible for your eyelids as it causes the oil glands that lubricate your eyes to atrophy and die. We are also going to release an eye drop with some pretty innovative features that aren’t on the market, such as aloe vera. Finally, we have plans to release an eye makeup line that again avoids the toxic preservative phenoxyethanol along with other ocular surface irritants. We are excited about this new opportunity to expand faster under the umbrella of a larger company. This means that more people suffering from dry, irritated eyes get to find relief by discovering us and our mission. Our 5-year plan is to reach over 1,000,000 people and learn, love, and fail a ton along the way. Have you read any good books in the last year? We love to read and listen to podcasts! We’re always listening to the Capitalism.com podcast with Ryan Daniel Moran, which is an amazing wealth of knowledge that’s allowed us to scale our business into the mid-seven figures. He recently came out with a new book, 12 Months to $1 Million, which details exactly what we did to grow our business from zero to what it is today. We followed his exact formula and haven’t looked back since. We also read Ready, Fire, Aim by Michael Masterson every single January. We do this because every time we read it, we find a new nugget of info to grow our business further. Lastly, every single business owner should dive into Profit First by Mike Michalowicz. This book changed our lives and how we run our business, and we recommend it to every business owner we meet. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? We’ve said this before, but our biggest piece of advice is to stop chasing the money and focus on people. Look for how you can serve others, and your business is much more likely to take off than if you’re constantly focused on the money. Also, sometimes you just have to make a decision. Pick one thing and run with it! Entrepreneurship is one decision after another and, oftentimes, the decisions aren’t easy. We all have a million things on our plate and there are a million different things you can focus on. However, sticking with a plan - such as whether to focus on Amazon or your website, who to sell to, etc - will allow you to serve that audience and see growth in your company. Of course, we all make bad decisions sometimes, but it’s often the case that we just need to focus to see results. Are you looking to hire for certain positions right now? Since we were just acquired, we’re not looking to hire anyone new right now. However, Eye Love has huge growth plans in the next three years, so we’re sure to be looking for more help soon! Where can we go to learn more? If you're interested in reading how they got started, published over 6 years ago, check it out here. Hello again! Remind us who you are and what business you started. Fredi is a wellness brand whose motto is “success at work starts with wellness”. We started Fredi after our Founder, Mitch’s experience on Wall Street, where he overworked himself to the point where he thought he needed to call an ambulance for himself after pulling a ridiculous amount of all-nighters (16 in 6 weeks). This experience made him realize he needed to start taking his health seriously, which sent him down a path of experimenting with a handful of wellness practices from meditation, to diet, to fitness. One of the products Mitch discovered during this journey was nootropics - supplements designed to boost cognitive function, especially things like focus, memory, and mood. Mitch found these products to be so effective and yet, no one around him had heard of them. After reaping the professional benefits of his new wellness practice, he decided he wanted to start a company around the concept and thought that an all-natural nootropic supplement would be the perfect product to enter the market with. This is when Fredi was born. Tell us about what you’ve been up to! Has the business been growing? We began selling our first product, Focused by Fredi, in April of 2020. It was a very scary period being the beginning of COVID, and we were delayed a few times by Amazon (our fulfillment partner) in simply getting our product to their warehouses in order for them to prioritize essential goods. Since then, we’ve had some major success with influencer marketing on TikTok and Instagram. Our product, which enhances cognitive function (namely focus, mood and memory), is something that’s of major interest to people who either have ADHD or experience the symptoms of it (which I believe we all do). Several of our customers have taken to TikTok and Instagram organically to speak about their experience with our product and how much it’s helped them. One of these TikTok testimonials back in December actually resulted in us selling over 2500 units in about 2 weeks, resulting in about $125k in revenue and sending us out of stock. The video only received about 450k views, which shows how engaged the TikTok community is. When we went out of stock, we, unfortunately, faced some manufacturer capacity issues and were forced to scramble to find a new manufacturer. This resulted in a 3-month out of the stock period that killed the momentum we had built. The only thing that helped us retain some of those customers was a 20% pre-order discount on our website - which was helpful in allowing us to hit the ground running one back in stock (we sent out about 500 pre-orders the second we were back in stock). The unfortunate thing about Amazon, however, is that when you’re out of stock, your product is simply delisted from the platform - which means we were unable to direct any Amazon customers toward our website or even just let them know we were out of stock… we simply just disappeared. Now that we’ve been back in stock, we’ve had a few more mini-viral hits that have helped us slowly build our momentum back. When we finally were back in stock at the end of March, we only had about 35 monthly subscribers to our product (we offer a 15% discount and free shipping for subscriptions) and now, by mid July, we have over 130. We’re now back up to doing about $25k a month in revenue and have done well over $250k in sales in the last 12 months. What have been your biggest lessons learned in the last year? Going viral is full of pros and cons. Don’t get me wrong - it’s a problem you want. Free awareness is the name of the game, especially after the new IOS update where paid ads are significantly less effective. When we went viral and then went out of stock, we lost all of that momentum we had been blessed with. I estimate we would have an additional 100-200 subscribers had we still had product to sell. An extra $5k-$10k in recurring revenue is truly game changing for a young business and something we’d obviously wish we didn’t have to forfeit. Additionally, something I’ve found very interesting is the difference in ACTUAL INFLUENCE among influencers. Some influencers have many followers and even good engagement… but their ability to drive traffic and conversions may be next to nothing. Other influencers may have way fewer followers, but usually, still good engagement and their ability to drive traffic and conversions is incredible. It’s a crazy game that takes a lot of experimenting and frankly, a lot of wasted marketing dollars. It’s not easy to drive real ROI in this category - despite what you may have read about. Find people through your network who can help you. Lastly, another lesson learned is that the heyday of digital marketing is over. People are tired of ads, and now the IOS update has restricted the data Facebook and other platforms have access to, you can’t even find the people who aren’t tired of those ads. The only way to solve this is by having incredibly creative and eye-catching ads - and even then it’s going to be tough to drive ROI. What’s in the plans for the upcoming year, and the next 5 years? We plan on onboarding some very strategic team members that can help drive awareness and build brand partnerships. We hope that this will get us to $1m in revenue and $5m in revenue the following year. We want to get very aggressive with building our team out with strategic people, who resonate with our brand message - even if it means giving up some equity. Have you read any good books in the last year? WiNNING by Tim Grover was a great read. It’s a great reminder that we should only expect to receive outsized gains through outsized effort and hustle. Advice for other entrepreneurs who might be struggling to grow their business? Get scrappy. Network. Find people through your network who can help you. Where can we go to learn more?
